title: Workers’ remittances reached $748.6 million in August 2026.
body_paragraphs: Inflows were nearly a tenth higher than a year earlier and only modestly below July, reinforcing the foreign‑exchange cushion as the currency weakened year‑to‑date. Elevated crude benchmarks above $100 a barrel kept import bills vulnerable, making household transfers a key buffer alongside exports and tourism.

Gross official reserves were provisionally estimated at $6.905 billion at end‑August, inclusive of the People’s Bank of China swap arrangement. The exchange rate had depreciated 5.7% by September 11, while the merchandise trade deficit widened on costlier fuel even as services receipts and inward transfers helped ease stress in the domestic forex market.

title: Cabinet approved the Rs. 46.19 billion Mudun Ela storm‑drainage and environment improvement project.
body_paragraphs: Implementation was scheduled over 2027–2036 to reduce chronic flooding in urban areas north of the capital. The plan drew on a Japan International Cooperation Agency pre‑feasibility study and a subsequent Sri Lanka Land Development Corporation assessment to free land for development.

The works target the Mudun Ela sub‑catchment, where waterlogging has impeded economic activity. By minimising flood damage in Peliyagoda and Kelaniya, the scheme aims to unlock stalled projects and lower disaster‑response costs for local authorities.

title: Sri Lanka inaugurated its first grid‑scale Battery Energy Storage System and a floating solar plant.
body_paragraphs: The storage facility in the North Central Province and the ‘Diya Janani’ array on Ibbankatuwa Reservoir are part of the national renewable programme. Grid‑side batteries (BESS, batteries that store electricity to balance supply and demand) were commissioned to improve stability and absorb variable generation.

The reservoir‑based photovoltaics are intended to add daytime energy without land acquisition. Officials said the additions support the long‑term target to raise clean‑power shares and reduce reliance on imported fuel in the generation mix.

title: Railway trade unions launched a 48‑hour strike on September 17.
body_paragraphs: Passenger services were disrupted nationwide as unions demanded a leadership change and withdrawal of a disciplinary letter to a station‑masters’ official. The subject minister said he could not accede to the removal request, leaving the core dispute unresolved as action commenced.

Ticket issuance was halted at some locations, allowing commuters to travel free of charge on certain services. Controllers, operating staff and station grades joined the stoppage, while organisers warned of further action if administrative and passenger‑service issues were not addressed.

title: Cabinet cleared publication of the 2027 Appropriation Bill and its presentation to Parliament.
body_paragraphs: The draft had earlier received clearance from the Attorney General following preparation by the Legal Draftsman. The proposal was tabled by the Finance Minister in his capacity overseeing planning and economic development.
Gazette publication will precede legislative debate as per constitutional procedure. The move follows cabinet approval in June to begin work on next year’s fiscal framework.

title: Sri Lanka and Thailand signed labour pacts and moved to expedite visa‑free travel for ordinary passports.
body_paragraphs: The agreements in Bangkok set a structured process for recruiting and protecting workers, with an initial intake of 10,000 positions approved to address shortages. Discussions also covered tourism, trade and maritime security as both sides sought to deepen people‑to‑people links.
Officials said the proposed visa exemption would facilitate two‑way travel while labour mobility will proceed under standard contracts, legal protections and repatriation arrangements.

title: Two children were killed in a grenade attack on a house in Dehiwala.
body_paragraphs: Investigators said the device was thrown at the wrong residence during a feud linked to organised crime, and two suspects were later arrested. The father was seriously injured as police reviewed CCTV and tracked movements connected to the incident.
Police stated the intended target was a nearby dwelling reportedly associated with a drug network, and that further arrests were expected as inquiries continued.

title: Government allocated Rs. 2.5 billion more to the Paddy Marketing Board for the Yala procurement drive.
body_paragraphs: Authorities said purchases had already exceeded original targets, prompting a reimbursement top‑up to continue buying in harvesting districts and Mahaweli zones. Actual collections were reported to have more than doubled the planned volumes in storage.

Ampara accounted for a major share of intake as allocations under the Agriculture Ministry’s fund were drawn down. Officials said the additional outlay would prevent interruptions while fields in remaining areas are reaped.

title: Polgolla Reservoir will be emptied for gate repairs from September 25; Kotmale generation will pause overnight September 26–27.
body_paragraphs: The dewatering window runs for roughly two and a half days to facilitate maintenance on control structures, with a parallel shutdown at the upstream hydro station. Residents relying on associated schemes were advised to use water sparingly during the operation.
Engineers scheduled the outage to minimise system risk while preserving safety margins, noting that power output would resume once works conclude.

title: Tea production in August fell 3.7% year‑on‑year to 19.00 million kilogrammes.
body_paragraphs: High‑ and medium‑grown categories contracted by double digits while the dominant low‑grown segment edged higher and made up nearly 69% of monthly output. Cumulative output for the first eight months was down 2.7% from last year.
Compared with August 2024, total manufacture was 11% lower, reflecting continued lag in key elevations despite modest gains in green tea volumes.
